findingDetails.title: Prompt text can forge command-owned deep-loop provenance
findingDetails.scopeProof: The shared core controls loop-repeat enforcement for all task-dispatch adapters and checks no provenance outside prompt text.
findingDetails.recommendation: Require runtime-owned provenance tied to externalized iteration state before granting the command-driven exemption.
findingDetails.claim: A direct Task caller can avoid loop-repeat rejection by inserting a syntactically valid iteration marker into its prompt.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Inspected marker bounds, target/mode resolution, persistence, adapters, and tests for runtime-owned identity or state verification.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The marker is expected to be emitted only by the parent command.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Runtime-owned unforgeable provenance plus a forged-marker rejection regression.

findingDetails.title: Dispatch audit persists credential formats outside its heuristic allowlist
findingDetails.scopeProof: Every runtime adapter uses the shared raw-command formatter; a JWT reproduction survives unchanged.
findingDetails.recommendation: Persist an allowlisted structural command summary rather than raw prompt text and restrict log permissions.
findingDetails.claim: A credential embedded in prompt prose can be written verbatim to the persistent audit log when it misses the fixed redaction patterns.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Reviewed all scrub patterns, tests, truncation, gitignore, and log-write behavior for generic credentials.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The local gitignored log is bounded and known credential spellings are redacted.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Raw prompt omission or comprehensive redaction and restrictive-mode tests that defeat the reproduction.
